transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it’s nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm explaining this right, I really don't want to waste your time. 

I guess what finally brought me in is that I’ve just been feeling a little... well, nothing too terrible, honestly, but just a bit disconnected lately. It’s like the part of me that used to reach out for people has just gone very quiet. I usually take so much pleasure in my work—I'm a social worker, so I'm used to being very engaged with others—and I've always loved my yoga classes, going to art galleries, or even just sitting down and journaling. But recently, I don't know, I'm mostly just... moving through my obligations, I suppose. 

I know everyone gets burnt out and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, but it just feels like I've lost my spark and I can't quite force it back. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you're looking for.
Have you found that things you usually enjoy no longer feel pleasurable?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say they aren't pleasurable at all. I really hope I didn't give you the wrong impression! I definitely still appreciate a good yoga class or a beautiful painting once I'm actually there. It's not like I'm completely numb... I'd hate for you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself, because I'm really not. 

It's just... maybe a little harder to feel that initial pull to go do them? But the enjoyment is definitely still there once I get started, I promise. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Did these feelings start after a particular stressful event or change in your life?

Oh, well... I wouldn't call it a *stressful* event, really. I mean, family is family, right? It’s a privilege to be able to help. But... I guess there was a bit of a change in my routine. About eight months ago, we took my older relative into our apartment to live with us. 

It’s been fine, really, I don't want to sound ungrateful or like they're a burden at all! But I suppose... yes, if I really step back and look at it, that's roughly when I started noticing this shift. This whole change in how I’m thinking, and working, and... well, just connecting with people. It's been going on for about eight months now, ever since they moved in. 

I hope I'm not making it sound like it's their fault, because it's really not, it's just an adjustment. I just want to make sure I'm answering your question correctly. Is that the kind of timeline you were asking about?
Have you been worrying excessively about things on most days?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've been worrying excessively. I mean, I have the usual concerns anyone would have, especially with a new living situation and my job, but I'm definitely not sitting around wringing my hands all day! I really try to stay positive and keep things in perspective. 

I hope I don't come across as someone who just complains and worries all the time, because I really try to be resilient. I just... I might overthink things a tiny bit sometimes, just wanting to make sure everyone is comfortable and happy, but it's nothing I can't handle. Does that make sense? I hope that's a helpful answer.
Do you feel this change in your mood and energy is mainly because of your older relative moving in and the responsibilities that came with that?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say it's mainly because of them at all. I mean, I really don't want to give the impression that I'm blaming them or that taking care of them is this huge, unbearable burden. I'm a social worker, you know? Helping people is what I do, and I'm honestly glad to have them with us. 

I think... well, it's just a coincidence, really, that things started feeling a little different around that time. The responsibilities are totally manageable, I promise. I just don't want you to think I'm overwhelmed by my own family or anything like that. I'm handling it fine! It's just... I don't really know exactly why I've been feeling this way, to be honest. I hope that's okay to say? I just want to make sure I'm not painting the wrong picture of my home life.
Have you been feeling down or sad most days?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've been feeling down or sad. I mean, everyone has a slightly off day here and there, right? But I'm definitely not walking around feeling depressed or anything like that. 

I really try to keep a smile on my face and bring good energy to my clients and my family. I wouldn't want to bring anyone else down, you know? So, no, I wouldn't use the word sad to describe how I've been feeling. I hope that's the kind of information you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Do you feel emotionally drained?

Um... I don't know if drained is exactly the right word, because I really am keeping up with everything, I promise. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just giving up or dropping the ball with my clients or my family. 

But... I guess what finally brought me in to see you is that... well, it’s a little hard to admit, especially being in the mental health field myself, but I feel like the part of me that used to really reach out for people, or take pleasure in things like my work, or my yoga classes, going to art galleries... even just my journaling... it’s all just gone very quiet lately. I’m mostly just moving through my obligations right now. I mean, I'm still getting them all done, of course! It's just... without that usual spark. I hope it's okay to admit that? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions correctly and giving you what you need.
Do you feel burned out?

Oh, um... burnout? No, I really don't think so. I mean, being in the field myself, I definitely know what professional burnout looks like, and I'm very careful to monitor myself so I don't get to that point. I would hate for my clients or my agency to ever feel like I'm not pulling my weight, you know? 

I'm still very committed to my work and my family. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm just throwing my hands up or that I can't handle my caseload. I'm trying my absolute best to stay on top of everything, and I really am getting it all done! So, no, I wouldn't use the phrase burned out at all. 

I just... I hope it's alright that I'm saying no to that? I want to be as helpful as possible for you to figure this out, so I hope I'm giving you the right information. Am I answering these the way you need me to?
Has this change made it harder for you to function well at work or at home?

Oh... well, I am absolutely still showing up to work every day. I wouldn't ever just abandon my responsibilities, I promise. But... um... I guess if I'm being completely honest—and I really want to give you the full picture here—it has been a little harder lately. 

I've actually... well, I missed a couple of grant deadlines recently. Which is so unlike me, I usually have everything color-coded and submitted early! And my supervisor—she's incredibly supportive—she’s quietly moved a few of my more demanding clients over to other clinicians. I think she just noticed I’m maybe not functioning at my absolute usual level right now, even though I'm really trying my best. 

I feel awful about it, honestly, letting my team down like that. I really hope it’s okay that I’m sharing this with you? I know it probably doesn't sound great, especially for a social worker, but I just want to make sure I'm being totally transparent and giving you exactly what you need to know. Does that help answer your question?
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Oh, sleeping? Um... no, actually, I've been sleeping just fine. I know how important sleep hygiene is—I mean, I preach it to my own clients all the time, right? So I really make it a point to get my full eight hours every night. I haven't noticed any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep at all. 

I... I hope it's okay that I don't have anything to report for that one? I know sleep issues are usually a big part of these kinds of assessments, so I just want to make sure it's alright that my sleep is normal and I'm just saying no. Is that okay?
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy?

Um... tired? No, I wouldn't say unusually so. I mean, I have my normal days where I feel a little drained after a long shift, but that's just the nature of the work, isn't it? I still have plenty of energy to get through my day, and I always make sure to keep up with my routine. 

I'm really trying to make sure I don't let myself get run down, so I've been staying pretty active and keeping my energy levels up. I definitely wouldn't want you to think I'm just lying in bed all day or anything like that! 

So, no, energy hasn't been a problem at all. I... I hope that's an okay answer? I know sometimes people expect to hear that I'm exhausted with everything else going on, so I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling guilty or like you've let people down?

Guilty? Um... well, I mean, maybe a little bit? Just with work, like I mentioned before with my supervisor taking on some of my clients. But I wouldn't say it's an overwhelming feeling of guilt or anything. I know I'm doing my best, and I try to remind myself of that. 

I definitely don't walk around feeling like a burden or like I'm constantly letting everyone down. I really try to stay positive and focus on what I *can* do, you know? 

I... I hope it's alright that I don't have a stronger answer for that. I know guilt can be a big thing for some people, but I just want to be honest that it's really not a major issue for me right now. Is it okay that I'm just saying no to that one, for the most part?
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Concentrating? Um... no, not at all, actually. I've been able to focus really well. I mean, doing what I do, I absolutely have to be dialed in when I'm sitting with a client or writing up my assessments, right? So I always make sure I'm staying really sharp. I haven't noticed my mind wandering or having to re-read things or anything like that. 

I... I hope I'm not making your job harder by keeping on saying no to these? I know you have a thorough checklist to get through, and I really want to be as helpful and cooperative as I can be. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact right picture. Is it alright that my concentration is perfectly fine?
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?

Appetite? Oh, um... no, my appetite has been completely normal. I've been eating just fine. I always make sure to get my three meals in, especially because I know how important it is to keep my strength up for work. 

I haven't been skipping meals or overeating or anything like that. Just... very steady, very normal. I try to make healthy choices, too, so I'm definitely taking good care of myself in that department. 

I really hope it's okay that I don't have anything concerning to report there either. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your assessment. Am I doing okay with these questions? I just want to be a good patient for you.
Have you been feeling hopeless?

Hopeless? Oh, um... no. No, definitely not hopeless. I actually try to stay really optimistic about things. I mean, working in the field myself, I know how important it is to hold onto hope, right? You really have to model that for the clients. So I always try to focus on the positives and look forward to the future. 

I haven't felt like giving up or... or anything dark like that at all. I really hope it's alright that I'm doing okay in that area. I know you're asking these for a good reason, and I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your evaluation. Is it okay that I'm feeling pretty hopeful? I just want to make sure I'm answering these the right way for you.
Have you been feeling like you’re less worthwhile or not as good as you usually are?

Worthwhile? Oh, um, no, not at all. I haven't been feeling like that. I actually feel... I feel very capable and confident in what I do. I mean, my work is so important, and I know I bring a lot of value to my clients. I always make sure I'm giving them my absolute best. 

I haven't felt down on myself or... or less than, or anything like that. I really try to maintain a strong sense of self-worth. It's so crucial, especially in social work, you know? 

I... I hope it's not frustrating that I'm doing well with all of these things you're asking about. I know you're doing a very thorough assessment, and I really want to be a helpful participant in this process. Am I giving you the kind of answers you need? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job for you.
Have you started feeling more detached or less compassionate toward your clients than you used to?

Less compassionate? Oh, um... I would never want to say I'm less compassionate. I really do care about my clients, I promise. It's just... well, I guess this is actually what finally brought me in to see you. I've been a little ashamed to admit it, because I know I'm supposed to be the one helping them, but... I feel like the part of me that used to really reach for people has just gone very quiet. 

It's not just at work, either. The things I used to take so much pleasure in—my yoga practice, going to art galleries, even just journaling at home... it's all just sort of faded out. I'm still doing everything I'm supposed to do, of course! I'm mostly just moving through my obligations right now, making sure everyone else is taken care of. 

I really hope I don't sound like a terrible social worker by admitting that. I'm still doing my job, I just... the joy in it is really quiet right now. Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I'm sharing that with you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on so I can get back to being my best self for them.
Do you feel emotionally detached from the people in your personal life?

Detached from my personal life? Oh, um... no, definitely not. I really wouldn't say that. I know I just said things feel a little quiet for me lately, but I still love my family and my friends very much. I always make sure I'm there for them. 

I mean, I might not be the most energetic person in the room right now, but the feelings are absolutely still there. I really pride myself on being a good friend and staying connected to the people who matter. I haven't pushed anyone away or stopped caring about them at all. 

I hope it's okay that I'm drawing that distinction for you. I know it might sound a little contradictory with what I just said about my clients, but I just want to make sure I'm being as accurate as possible for your assessment. Is that the kind of detail you need? I really want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture.
Have you been crying more easily than usual?

Crying? Oh, um... no, I haven't been crying more easily. Not at all. 

I know I mentioned feeling a little... flat, or quiet, earlier, but it hasn't translated into tears or anything like that. I really try to keep my composure. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just falling apart or unable to handle things. I'm still managing my day-to-day very well, and I always make sure to keep a professional demeanor. 

I hope it's not a problem that I keep saying no to some of these things. I know you have a specific set of questions to get through, and I really want to be cooperative. Am I doing okay with these answers? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your notes.
When you're with your clients, do you feel emotionally distant from them?

Emotionally distant? Oh, I... well, I wouldn't use the word *distant*. That sounds so cold, doesn't it? I really, really try to make sure my clients feel heard and supported every single session. I would hate for them to ever think I wasn't fully present for them.

I mean, I did mention earlier that the... the reaching out part of me feels a bit quiet right now. So maybe I'm not feeling that deep, emotional pull in my chest the way I used to when they share something hard. But I'm still listening, and I'm still providing the right interventions. I'm just... experiencing it a little differently internally. 

I hope that makes sense? I just really don't want you to think I'm abandoning them emotionally. I'm still doing my very best for them. Is that... does that answer what you're asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
